Direct denominator counting for d=jp gives (p−1)Σφ(j), and the numerator kp contribution is T_k−L_k. Möbius inversion of the coprime d count gives |η_k|≤τ(k), thus f_p(mp)=pC_m+E_m and |E_m|≤m² whenever m<p. At the single new denominator mp the exact jump is (p−1)φ(m). An INDEPENDENT Fraction sieve over all m=3..820 confirms min C=6/5, min(φ−C)=1/2 and −9<C_820<−8. For p>2·820² the two error inequalities enforce all signs; 817 pairs and one last sample force 1634 sign transitions. This is a uniform infinite-prime proof based on an exhaustive FINITE m-range certificate, not a prime sample extrapolation.

originality.rationale: Qualified PASS: the 2015 Lagarias–Mehta analysis studies the same reduced Farey product, establishes general valuation identities and a short sign pattern through 3p−1 (Theorem 4.10); its Property (P3) is a much stronger but unproved fixed-prime claim. The audited certified 817 paired signs and the first failure of the prime-scale coefficient at 820 are new finite-window consequences not stated by that theorem, requiring a separate exact rational census. Historical earlier tabulations could cover the coefficient cutoff; that risk remains.
residual_risks: Older unpublished or unindexed exact Farey-valuation tables could include C_820 and many sign alternations.
Threshold p>1,344,800 is sufficient, not asserted optimal; result does not settle infinitely many signs for a fixed prime.

value.rationale: A rigorous large explicit window with 1634 successive nonzero sign alternations materially strengthens a sparse earlier local sign theorem for a canonical arithmetic product, while the first m=820 coefficient failure describes where that linear prime-scale mechanism ceases. The finite cutoff is structurally defined as the first failure, not an arbitrary slice; no infinitely-many-changes-for-fixed-p assertion is made.

final_claim: For every prime p>1,344,800, the reduced reciprocal Farey-product valuation has f_p(mp−1)<0<f_p(mp) for 3≤m≤819 and f_p(820p)<0, forcing at least 1634 strict changes in the displayed prime-scale window. The scaling coefficient C_m=2Σ_{j≤m}φ(j)−mΣφ(j)/j stays strictly between 0 and φ(m) for 3≤m≤819 and first leaves that interval at m=820.
limitations: Older unpublished or unindexed exact Farey-valuation tables could include C_820 and many sign alternations.
Threshold p>1,344,800 is sufficient, not asserted optimal; result does not settle infinitely many signs for a fixed prime.
